name: Checkpoint Flag
description: Ordered respawn markers that turn one long level into a series of short commitments. Each flag owns its place in the order and the respawn placement; the set of flags shares one 'furthest reached' fact so a later flag never loses progress to an earlier one the player brushed past on the way back. It deliberately does not own death detection — world.hazard_volume already reports world.hazard_entered, and a second death definition would double every kill downstream. It also does not reset the run: health, inventory, and collectibles are their own components' state, and which of them a death should roll back is a game-level decision, not a flag's. Cross-session persistence of the reached checkpoint belongs to persistence.save_system, not to this component.

inputs.name: checkpointOrder
inputs.description: This flag's position in the level sequence. Order, not distance, decides which checkpoint is active — flags placed on a backtrack route must still sort by intended progression.

inputs.name: respawnOffset
inputs.description: Where the player reappears relative to the flag. Slightly above and clear of the trigger volume, so respawning never immediately reactivates the flag or an adjacent hazard.

inputs.name: singleActivation
inputs.description: Whether the flag fires progression.checkpoint_reached only the first time. Re-fireable flags let speedrun routing re-arm respawn points, at the cost of noisier downstream counting.

inputs.name: respawnDelaySeconds
inputs.description: Pause between the hazard event and repositioning. Instant respawns hide what killed the player; long ones punish. One second is the genre's reading of 'fair'.

outputs.name: isActive
outputs.description: True only on the furthest-reached flag — the single source of the respawn point for the whole level.
